lead.t: Fournier's gangrene: radical debridement of the scrotal and perineal skin; faecal diversion (colostomy) if the anorectum is involved; suprapubic or urethral catheter for urinary diversion; orchidectomy is rarely needed.

snip.t: Fournier's gangrene: radical debridement of the scrotal and perineal skin; faecal diversion (colostomy) if the anorectum is involved; suprapubic or urethral catheter for urinary diversion; orchidectomy is rarely needed.
Scrotal complaints: swelling, pain, skin lesions (Fournier's gangrene), an absent or retractile testis.

snip.t: Named forms: Fournier's gangrene (the genital, perineal and perianal region), Ludwig's angina (the submandibular and sublingual spaces), Meleney's ulcer (progressive bacterial synergistic gangrene of the abdominal wall), and gas gangrene (clostridial myonecrosis).
Do not aspirate a hydrocele of uncertain cause because of the risk of tumour seeding and infection (even Fournier's gangrene has been reported).
